free_text.computational: Skills in lab - practical skills (6 practicals), experimental design, troubleshooting, critical analysis, and scientific writing are core outcomes. The module also strengthens presentation skills and report writing.
free_text.lab:
Critical skills developed include standard microbiology, DNA/protein extraction, PCR/qPCR, protein purification, colorimetric assays, and gel electrophoresis. 

Environmental quality assessments are not covered, as this is a molecular lab-based module.
free_text.personal:
The module places strong emphasis on scientific communication, critical thinking, project development, reliability, and attention to detail.

Team roles are used to encourage leadership fundamentals and collaborative practice, and time management is key as we organised several round tables around their project development as a team (key for their future career in molecular biology).
free_text.knowledge:
Biotechnology – core to this module: recombinant DNA, molecular tools, qPCR, protein expression. From Standard to Advanced molecular tools

Microbiology – working with microbial systems for molecular techniques.

Experimental Design & Data Interpretation – critical reasoning, replication, use of controls, and critical data analysis troubleshooting, method optimisation.

Ecotoxicology – applying molecular tools to study pollutant effects at cellular and organismal levels (e.g., sunscreen filters, plastics).

Disease Biomarkers – identifying and analysing molecular markers of disease, with direct applications in biomedical contexts.

Neurodegenerative Diseases, Aging & Oxidative Stress – exploring molecular pathways of oxidative damage and their roles in aging and disorders such as Alzheimer’s or Parkinson’s, alongside applications in both biomedical and environmental toxicology.

modules.name: Lab Essentials for Physical & Life Sciences

free_text.lab: SCIU3LS provides first exposure to basic lab skills that will be used in later modules.
free_text.personal:
This module is often students’ very first structured lab group experience. Because of this, we do not assume that students already possess advanced teamwork, communication, or time-management skills especially in a laboratory setting.

Teamwork basics – students are introduced to working in pairs or small groups at the bench, with clear instructions on sharing tasks and supporting one another.

Communication protocols – guidance is provided on how to communicate effectively with lab partners and demonstrators, including safety-related reporting.

Time management – activities are designed with strict timeframes, helping students practice planning their work within the lab session.

Professional conduct – reliability, attendance, punctuality, and respect for shared equipment are highlighted as core responsibilities.
free_text.knowledge:
Basic Laboratory Safety (risk awareness, lab conduct, COSHH basics)

Quantitative Reasoning (basic calculations for concentrations, dilutions, pH, thermodynamics, physics)

Introduction to Experimental Design (controls, replication, systematic lab methods)

free_text.field:
The SCIU3FB module teaches a range of field skills, including plant identification and diversity indices, aquatic invertebrate identification, animal footprint and sign recognition, bird identification and ecology, as well as survey methods for monitoring purposes. Students are also introduced to research questions, hypotheses and predictions, and experimental design, enabling them to acquire essential research skills.

Through mini-projects, students further develop field skills that vary depending on the project they choose. These projects are always ecological in nature and focus on survey-based studies of fauna and flora on campus.
free_text.personal: Some interpersonal skills are difficult to teach directly or provide step-by-step instructions for. Instead, giving students the opportunity to develop these skills requires creating the right environment and fostering an inclusive atmosphere where they can engage meaningfully. Certain resources developed by Joshua may also play a critical role in supporting the development of these skills.
